issues.legal_issue: A family settlement relinquishing interests in immovable property may be established by an oral arrangement, with an unregistered written record serving as evidence of an arrangement already made.
material_facts: Two claimants signed a village-panchayat resolution stating that they had relinquished their interests in two properties in exchange for consideration, and evidence supported that payments were made.
The resolution was unregistered, but the court found that it recorded a family settlement already reached between the family members.
The parties’ subsequent conduct, including living separately and not seeking partition for a period, supported the settlement.
issues.conclusion: The claimants had relinquished their interests in the two properties, and the partition claim concerning those properties was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 17 and 49 of the Registration Act, 1908, a writing that itself creates or extinguishes interests in immovable property generally requires registration and, if unregistered, cannot prove the transaction affecting the property. An oral family settlement is not required to be registered; an unregistered writing recording an earlier oral settlement may be used as corroborative evidence to explain the settlement and the parties’ conduct. Section 91 of the Evidence Act, 1872, does not make such an unregistered writing proof of a transaction that required registration. No earlier case was cited on this issue.

rule.if: partition_appeal and oral_family_settlement and unregistered_record_memorializes_prior_settlement and settlement_record_signed_by_participants and consideration_paid and conduct_supports_settlement

predicates.partition_appeal: The dispute is before the court in an appeal arising from a partition proceeding.
predicates.oral_family_settlement: The family members had reached an oral arrangement concerning their interests in the property.
predicates.unregistered_record_memorializes_prior_s: A written record was unregistered and recorded an arrangement already reached, rather than itself being intended to create the arrangement.
predicates.settlement_record_signed_by_participants: The participants in the arrangement signed the written record.
predicates.consideration_paid: The person receiving the property paid consideration to the persons relinquishing their interests.
predicates.conduct_supports_settlement: The parties’ subsequent conduct was consistent with the arrangement having been made and acted upon.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a partition claim and the facts show that an oral family settlement was recorded, supported by payment and subsequent conduct, the claim to shares covered by that settlement is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may interfere with concurrent findings when the courts below have palpably misappreciated or ignored material evidence and their findings are inconsistent with the record.
material_facts: The trial court and High Court had both rejected the alleged relinquishment of interests in two properties.
The Supreme Court found that those courts had brushed aside oral and documentary evidence supporting the settlement and had ignored material facts and the parties’ conduct.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent findings concerning the two properties were palpably erroneous and were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court’s power under Article 136 of the Constitution is exercised sparingly and in furtherance of justice, but permits review where findings are perverse or grossly or palpably erroneous, inconsistent with the material on record, or reached through perfunctory treatment of evidence. The Court relied on Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation v. P.H. Brahmbhatt, (1974) 3 SCC 601; (1974) 2 SCR 128.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and concurrent_findings and material_evidence_ignored and findings_palpably_inconsistent_with_record

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The matter is before the Supreme Court in an appeal invoking its special appellate jurisdiction.
predicates.concurrent_findings: The courts below reached the same findings on the disputed issue.
predicates.material_evidence_ignored: The courts below failed to consider or properly weigh material oral or documentary evidence.
predicates.findings_palpably_inconsistent_with_reco: The findings cannot reasonably be reconciled with the evidence and material facts on the record.

issues.definition: When an appeal presents concurrent findings that ignore material evidence and are palpably inconsistent with the record, those findings are set aside.

issues.legal_issue: Land possessed and cultivated by a family and regularized in one family member’s name for the family’s benefit remains family property where the application for regularization preceded the family’s division.
material_facts: Evidence showed that the family’s father possessed and cultivated the land and that the family continued its cultivation after his death.
The defendant managed the family affairs and applied for regularization of the land before the family members had divided their status.
The land was regularized in the defendant’s name after the partition suit was filed, and the evidence did not establish that he had encroached upon and cultivated it individually.
issues.conclusion: The land was granted for the benefit of the family and was family property; all five family members were entitled to equal shares.
issues.legal_principle: The character of the land depended on the evidence of its possession, cultivation, and the circumstances in which it was regularized. A grant made in one family member’s name for the benefit of the undivided family does not make the land that member’s self-acquired property. The court rejected the reliance on Thimmegowda v. Siddegowda, ILR 1991 Karnataka 4506, as a basis for treating the land as joint family property solely because the defendant had not proved the source of the payment; its conclusion rested on the evidence that the family possessed and cultivated the land and that the application preceded division.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and family_possession_and_cultivation and regularization_application_before_family_division and individual_acquisition_not_established and grant_in_one_member_name

predicates.partition_proceeding: The dispute concerns division of property claimed to belong to a family.
predicates.family_possession_and_cultivation: The family, rather than only the person named in the grant, possessed and cultivated the land.
predicates.regularization_application_before_family: The application to regularize the land was made while the family remained undivided.
predicates.individual_acquisition_not_established: The evidence did not establish that the named applicant acquired and cultivated the land in an individual capacity.
predicates.grant_in_one_member_name: The authorities granted the land in the name of only one family member.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding, land possessed and cultivated by an undivided family and regularized in one member’s name after an application made before division is treated as family property when individual acquisition is not established, and the family members receive equal shares.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant’s statement that they do not wish to claim a share does not transfer that share to other family members when no written relinquishment has been made.
material_facts: Two claimants stated in their evidence that they were not interested in claiming shares in the land.
Neither claimant filed anything in writing directing that their shares be given to other family members.
The land was found to have been granted for the benefit of the family.
issues.conclusion: The two claimants remained entitled to equal shares in the land, though they could relinquish those shares in favour of other family members during the final-decree proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: A statement of lack of interest, without a written relinquishment of the share in favour of another person, did not divest the claimants of their shares in the circumstances of this case. No earlier case was cited on this issue.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and claimant_orally_disclaims_share and no_written_relinquishment_in_favour_of_others and property_belongs_to_family

predicates.partition_proceeding: The dispute concerns division of family property.
predicates.claimant_orally_disclaims_share: A claimant states orally or in evidence that they are not interested in receiving a share.
predicates.no_written_relinquishment_in_favour_of_o: The claimant has not made a written relinquishment directing that the share pass to another person.
predicates.property_belongs_to_family: The property is held to be family property.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding, a claimant who orally disclaims a share in family property but has not made a written relinquishment in favour of others retains a share.
